validated_results.reason: The study examines GPX1 Pro198Leu genotype and erythrocyte glutathione peroxidase enzyme activity rather than nutritional glutathione exposure, so the requested exposure is another concept.

validated_results.title: Soy isoflavones augment the effect of TRAIL-mediated apoptotic death in prostate cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: This is an in vitro experiment in LNCaP prostate cancer cells assessing apoptosis, with no human participants or incident cancer outcome.

validated_results.title: Soy isoflavones augment the effect of TRAIL-mediated apoptotic death in prostate cancer cells.
validated_results.reason: The soy isoflavone exposure was applied only to cultured prostate cancer cell lines, making it an exclusively preclinical study.

validated_results.title: Intake of whole-grain products and risk of prostate cancer among men in the Danish Diet, Cancer and Health cohort study.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort of Danish men reporting an adjusted incidence rate ratio for total whole-grain product intake and incident prostate cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Continuous, per 50 g/day of total whole-grain product intake
extraction.population: Men aged 50-64 years in the Diet, Cancer and Health cohort

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 26,691 men aged 50-64 years participated in the Diet, Cancer and Health cohort study and provided information about diet and potential prostate cancer risk factors. During a median follow-up of 12.4 years, we identified 1,081 prostate cancer cases.

cases.excerpt: During a median follow-up of 12.4 years, we identified 1,081 prostate cancer cases.

effect_size.excerpt: Overall, there was no association between total intake of whole-grain products and prostate cancer risk (adjusted incidence rate ratio per 50 g day(-1): 1.00 (95% confidence interval: 0.96, 1.05)) as well as between intake of the specific whole-grain products: whole-grain rye bread, whole-grain bread, and oatmeal, and risk of prostate cancer. No risk estimates did differ according to either stage or grade of disease.

validated_results.title: The correlation between zinc and insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), its binding protein (IGFBP-3) and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) in prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: The study correlates plasma zinc with IGF-1, IGFBP-3 and PSA levels in already-diagnosed patients to propose early diagnostic markers, providing no evidence on prostate cancer incidence.
